name: User Accounts
description: Lets people create an account and log in securely.
proof: created a test account, signed in as them, then deleted it

name: File Storage
description: Lets people upload and store files (like photos), and get them back later.
proof: stored a test file, read it back unchanged, then removed it

name: Structured Data
description: A place to save and look up structured information, like user profiles or orders.
proof: saved a test record, looked it back up, then removed it

name: Background Job
description: Runs a small piece of work in the background (like resizing a photo) without making the user wait.
proof: ran it once with test input and it finished successfully

name: Send Email
description: Sends an email to a user, like a confirmation or welcome message.
proof: sent a test email and confirmed it went out

name: Scheduled Task
description: Runs something automatically on a schedule, like a weekly digest email.
proof: checked that the schedule is set and active

name: Background Queue
description: Lines up work to be done in the background so nothing gets lost or slows the app down.
proof: checked that the work queue is up and ready

name: Push Notifications
description: Sends an alert or notification out to users or to other parts of the app when something happens.
proof: checked that the notification sender is up and ready

name: App Secrets
description: Stores sensitive values (like a third-party API key) safely instead of hardcoding them in the app.
proof: checked that the secure storage is up and ready

name: App Settings
description: Stores small configuration values the app can read, like feature flags or simple settings.
proof: checked that the settings store is up and answering

name: Backend API
description: Gives your app a backend it can call over the internet to do server-side logic.
proof: checked that the backend is up and answering

name: Search
description: Lets users search through content in your app.
proof: checked that search is up and ready

name: Multi-Step Workflow
description: Runs a multi-step process in order -- like checking a signup, sending a welcome email, then logging the result.
proof: ran the whole process once end-to-end and every step finished
